properties.title: Port Sudan: night lights 45% below its recent nights (NASA Black Marble, 27 Nov 2026)
properties.summary: NASA's Black Marble (near real time, NOAA-20) gives 0.76 nW/cm²/sr over a box about 44 km across Port Sudan on the night of 27 Nov 2026, 45% below the median of the 10 clear nights in the 14 before it (1.39). 80% of the box was clear, so part of the city went unmeasured that night. A drop in light fits a grid failure, strikes on the grid, rationing or load shedding, and also smoke, dust or snow the cloud mask missed; Blackout measures how much darker it was, not why. NASA advises against using near-real-time data for tactical decisions or local-scale conditions.

baseline_ref.window: median of the counted nights (at least 60% of the box clear) in the 14 nights before, at least 5 of them (BO-IND-15)

sources.publisher: NASA (Black Marble, VIIRS on NOAA-20; near real time from NASA LANCE, standard from LAADS DAAC)
sources.title: VJ146A2 Gap-Filled Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights Daily
sources.licence: NASA Earth science data: no restrictions on use, citation requested (Black Marble VJ146A2, DOI 10.5067/VIIRS/VJ146A2.002, and its near-real-time version from NASA LANCE); near-real-time data are provided as is under the LANCE disclaimer
sources.descriptor: Night radiance with moonlight and surface effects removed, about 500 m pixels, one pass a night. Blackout averages the clear pixels in a box about 44 km across each watched city.

properties.title: Cloudflare: 31 public Bluesky posts report it down or out in 6 h (usual 3.4)
properties.summary: Members of the public posted 31 times on Bluesky naming "Cloudflare" with "down" (19) or "outage" (12) in the 6 hours to 09:46 UTC 28 Nov 2026, against a usual of 3.4 for that many hours over the 7 days before. Posts rose past the line in the hour from 04:46 UTC 28 Nov 2026 and peaked in the hour from 06:46 UTC 28 Nov 2026. Reported by the public on Bluesky and not confirmed by Cloudflare; Blackout counts the posts and does not read or keep them. Blackout does not assess its cause. A surge can also be news of an outage elsewhere that names the company, a joke, the words in another sense, or the company's own denial (BO-H-7B).

baseline_ref.window: rolling: the same two searches over the 7 days before the 6-hour window, scaled to 6 hours (the usual taken as at least the floor)

sources.title: Posts naming the service with "down" or "outage": counts only
sources.licence: No data licence stated; Blackout keeps and republishes only post counts and a link to Bluesky's own search, never a post, its text or its author (Bluesky's developer guidelines ask apps to honour deletions)
sources.descriptor: How many public Bluesky posts named the service with an outage word: what members of the public said, unverified, never what the company said.

properties.summary: Cloudflare Radar's hijack detection lists event 174609 at confidence 12 (Cloudflare's high band is 8 and above), first seen 2026-11-25T09:26:41Z, last seen 2026-11-25T10:46:14Z, by 50 of Radar's 280 route-collector peers.
